title: Cavity Magnetron Basics
text: A cavity magnetron generates microwaves from electrons moving in a magnetic field. An eight-cavity magnetron usually runs in the pi mode for stable output. Cavity magnetrons were developed in 1940 for radar.

title: Cavity Magnetron Basics (mirror)
text: A cavity magnetron generates microwaves from electrons moving in a magnetic field. An eight-cavity magnetron usually runs in the pi mode for stable output. Cavity magnetrons were developed in 1940 for radar.

title: History of the Cavity Magnetron
text: The cavity magnetron was developed in 1940 at the University of Birmingham. Its microwave output made compact airborne radar possible. An eight-cavity magnetron runs in the pi mode, where adjacent cavities oscillate in opposite phase.

title: Reflex Klystron
text: A reflex klystron is a single-cavity microwave oscillator. The repeller electrode reflects the electron beam back through the cavity. Output frequency can be tuned electronically by changing the repeller voltage.

title: Klystron Oscillation Modes
text: A reflex klystron is a single-cavity oscillator with a repeller. Electronic tuning of a reflex klystron is done by changing the repeller voltage, which shifts the frequency within each mode.
